metadata.case_name: MAK YIU KEUNG v. HO CHEUNG KAT

plaintiff.occupation_after: stayed at home; assisted wife in preparing vegetables and did cutting threads for a clothing factory
plaintiff.education_level: limited education; lack of knowledge of English

injuries.description: Near-complete amputation / severe traumatic injury to left wrist and hand resulting in a useless left hand
source: the saw, which had no guard, came into contact with his left wrist and hand, cutting it to such an extent that his left hand was almost completely amputated.
his left hand...is clawed and scarred, has no movement at all and with extensive sensory loss,
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of wrist or hand, unspecified

manifestations.description: Clawed and scarred left hand (cosmetic deformity)
No movement at all in left hand
Extensive sensory loss in left hand
Swelling in the hand in winter
Tendency for the hand to bruise easily
Unable to return to any employment requiring a degree of dexterity
Frustration and depression at not being able to secure regular employment and to provide for his family

treatments_received: re-amputation of the left little finger and fixation of fracture
subsequent removal of the Silastic rods
first of a number of reconstructive operations over the next few years
treatments_future: suggested amputation and fitting of a prosthesis (patient rejected further operation)

losses.description: Useless and almost amputated left hand causing severe functional impairment
Unsightly left hand and scarring causing embarrassment

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Prevents him from performing simple day to day tasks that a person with both hands takes for granted
Cannot return to skilled carpentry or any employment requiring dexterity

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer play badminton with his children
Unable to provide for his family as he had before his accident

comparable_cases.case_name: Chun Yat Nam v. Attorney General
comparable_cases.injury_description: Revised the level of awards for pain suffering and loss of amenities raising the substantial injury category to $335,000.00 to $415,000.00
